headline: UPDATE to totw-20261024-1900-03 (Hebron operation, day 2) -- 250 families evacuated overnight
dek: Haaretz: ~250 Palestinian families were evacuated from their homes overnight Friday into Saturday in the Hebron neighbourhood where Friday's two gunmen lived; families allowed only essential belongings; some went to a municipality reception centre, others to relatives; demolitions of structures…
sources: Hebron deputy mayor Khaled Fahed al-Qawasmi to Haaretz; Hebron Mayor Yousef al-Jaabari to WAFA; Netanyahu via Times of Israel and Al Jazeera liveblog
fault_line: 'Evacuation' vs 'forced displacement': AJ's own audience argues the wording while 250 families sleep out — security operation or election-eve collective punishment?

sections.what_happened: Haaretz: ~250 Palestinian families were evacuated from their homes overnight Friday into Saturday in the Hebron neighbourhood where Friday's two gunmen lived; families allowed only essential belongings; some went to a municipality reception centre, others to relatives; demolitions of structures begun. Times of Israel (local reports): ~1,500 displaced as of Saturday; WAFA/governor: 200+ families displaced, dozens spent the night outside, governorate declared a state of emergency; Mayor al-Jaabari to WAFA: forces seek to displace another 2,500 people from two areas. Displaced-count spread across sources (1,200 Reuters / 1,500 local / 2,200 mayor to AJ) reflects different counting moments and definitions, NOT a single agreed toll — report as a range with attribution, never a single number. Netanyahu vows a 'big surprise' for the Palestinian Authority (ToI) and, per AJ's Birzeit reporting, told supporters: 'When we win the election, we'll finish the job. We've completed 90 percent... that means bringing down the Iranian regime and finishing off Hamas and Hezbollah' — an election-eve war pledge spanning Lebanon, Syria, the West Bank, Gaza and Iran. Separately: WAFA via Haaretz — settlers attacked and wounded Palestinian farmers west of Hebron Saturday morning; AJ liveblog — Israeli forces fired stun grenades at Al Jazeera journalists documenting a bulldozing operation near the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint; Hamas called the West Bank attacks 'an extension of the criminal aggression' and demanded 'serious international action'; municipality head to Reuters: the operation is motivated by Tuesday's election, when Netanyahu's coalition may lose its majority ('trying to win as many votes as possible from the settlers').
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1), Haaretz (T3), Times of Israel (T3), Al Jazeera liveblog (T2, STATE QA), WAFA (T3, STATE PS) — distinct families agreeing on the operation's scale; counts differ by source and moment
sections.what_disputed: IDF: operation is 'focused and limited to the area from which the terrorists operated', searches for militants/weapons, demolitions of terror infrastructure; gunmen killed Friday after killing two soldiers. The election-motivation reading is the municipality head's claim, not an established IDF motive; polls showing the coalition may lose its majority are reported by Reuters without a named pollster in the item.
sections.why_matters: 250 families out overnight, 2,500 more in the crosshairs, and a prime minister promising to 'finish the job' three days before the vote — Hebron is now the election's front line.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE to totw-20261024-1900-03 (Hebron operation, day 2) -- 250 families evacuated overnight; mayor says forces seek to displace 2,500 more; Netanyahu vows 'big surprise' for PA and election-eve 'finish the job'

totw_analysis: Our read: 250 families out overnight, 2,500 more in the crosshairs, and a prime minister promising to 'finish the job' three days before the vote — Hebron is now the election's front line.
